news.headline: The World's Heaviest Pumpkin Becomes a Giant Jack-o'-Lantern
news.body: Remember the first pumpkin ever to weigh more than 3,000 pounds? Just in time for Halloween, a team of carvers in Salem, Massachusetts, turned it into the heaviest jack-o'-lantern of all time! They spent 32 hours carving flying bats, a witch with a knobbly nose, and a goofy skeleton. A Guinness World Records judge checked, and the carved pumpkin still weighed 3,156 pounds. That's about as heavy as a small car!

news.headline: Spacewalk No. 100 Gives the Space Station More Power
news.body: Astronauts Anil Menon and Joshua Kutryk floated outside the International Space Station for more than seven hours this week. It was the 100th spacewalk by an American astronaut crew! They unrolled a new solar panel, kind of like unrolling a giant yoga mat, to soak up sunlight and make electricity. One more panel will be added next week, and then the station will have about 30 percent more power.

news.headline: A Rare Amur Leopard Cub Is Growing Big and Strong
news.body: The Potawatomi Zoo in South Bend, Indiana, has a brand-new Amur leopard cub! The little boy cub was born in September, and he doesn't have a name yet. Zookeepers have been feeding him and caring for him around the clock, and he is growing healthy and strong. Amur leopards are some of the rarest big cats on Earth. Only about 100 live in the wild, so every new cub is a big deal.
